title: Lucena: building the bridge, play it out
outcomes: Plays out a won rook-and-pawn ending against the tablebase within a move budget
Says when a cut-off by a single file is too thin and the move decides
Separates won positions from rook-pawn draws before choosing a plan

steps.text: In **Lucena: building the bridge** and **Lucena: building the bridge, which positions win?** you built the bridge and checked the file. Here the cut-off is thin: a rook on the neighbouring file holds the enemy king back by a single file. The same placement can win or draw. Predict before you look.

steps.title: Same placement, who has the move?
steps.prompt: Predict each result, then check. The kings, rooks and pawn are identical.

steps.text: **Conditions.** In the positions here, a cut-off by a single file is enough when you have the move, and not enough when the defender has it. **When it fails:** a defender who moves first has a rook check, here Rg8+, that drives your king away from the pawn. Rule of thumb: when the cut-off is only one file wide, count who moves first.
Now play it out against the tablebase. Before your first move, decide what the bridge needs: a rook on the right rank, your king out of the check line. A sensible budget is the number of moves shown.

steps.prompt: In the games you played out, where did you spend moves on checks that gave nothing? What would you do first next time?
